sub.en: Look at the pairs. Which sentence says WHEN, and which one only says THAT it happened?

items.q: “Have you visited Brazil before?” — “Yes, I ___ — twice.”
items.why: Present perfect: the experience, with no finished time.  Past Simple: a finished time — in 2019, when I was a child, yesterday.

items.q: I ___ here when I was a child.

She ___ a marathon. (we don’t know when)
I ___ Star Wars twice this month. (the month isn’t finished)
I ___ Star Wars twice last month. (the month is finished)
“___ you ever been to a film festival?”

write.q: Bring the whole course together: write 8 sentences. Where you were born, what you do now, what your area is like, one thing you can’t do, one thing you’ve never done, one plan for next year, and one thing you did at a finished time in the past.
write.model: I was born in Karaganda in 1996 and I grew up there. I’m an engineer and I work freelance from home. My neighbourhood is quiet: there’s a library, but there aren’t any museums. I can’t drive, but I can ski. I’ve been to three music festivals, but I’ve never played an instrument. Next year I’m going to take a Spanish course on Saturdays. I went to my first concert in 2015, when I was nineteen. It was the best evening of that year.

speak.q: The final task. Speak for two minutes about your own year: where you were, what you do, what you’ve done that you’re proud of, what you’ve never done, and what you’re going to do next. Then make one phone call: ask for somebody, hear that they are not available, and leave a message.
speak.model: I was born in Karaganda and I live in Almaty now. I’m an engineer. This year I’ve finished a big project and I’ve been to two festivals. I’ve never travelled outside Central Asia — that’s the plan. Next year I’m going to save money and go to Georgia. — Hello, could I speak to Aigul, please? — I’m afraid she’s not available. — Can you tell her to call me back? My number is 8 701 233 45 67.
